dedupe_keys.name: global map of travel time to cities 2015 with friction surface

description: This global accessibility map gives, for every 1 km (30 arc-second) pixel, the travel time in minutes to the nearest high-density urban centre in 2015. It was made by assigning each pixel a movement speed in a friction surface and running a least-cost-path algorithm from every pixel to a set of high-density urban points; the friction surface, giving minutes needed to travel one metre, is published with the map so that users can compute accessibility to other point sets. The DANS record holds both GeoTIFF products in WGS 84 with ISO 19139 metadata and a description of how they were produced; it credits D. Weiss as author. Coverage is global. Access: free download from the DANS Physical and Technical Sciences Data Station under CC BY 4.0 (released June 2024); the friction surface is about 3 GB. Caveats: the map reflects 2015 networks and a modelled, not observed, travel speed. It supports global accessibility and equity analysis, estimation of detours when transport links fail and prioritisation of rural road investments, and complements the gridded 192-city transport dataset and the global roads data catalogued here.
name: Global map of travel time to cities, 2015, with friction surface
